transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Miguel Alvarez (Orchid Channel Lead), Priya Nair (Orchid AE), Jasper Cole (Orchid SE)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we got Miguel, Priya, Jasper from Orchid, and Ethan and I from Redwood. Is that right?
[00:08] Miguel: Yep, that's us. Thanks Samira.
[00:11] Samira: Cool, goal for today is a quick pipeline review and then dig into any technical or procurement blockers so we can land the co-sell pilots. Roughly 30 minutes for pipeline and 15 for tech. Sound good?
[00:22] Priya: Sounds perfect.
[00:25] Samira: Okay, Miguel, do you want to walk through the top three deals you flagged?
[00:30] Miguel: Sure. First up is Veridian Health — large hospital chain, pilot request for clinical summarization and coding. They care a lot about PHI, data residency, and audit logs. Target decision in 6 weeks. Second is Nimbus Retail — call center assistant for returns and policy lookup, mid-market, latency sensitive but no PHI. Third is Lattice Finance — fintech use case, accounts payable automation, needs SOC 2 and stronger encryption at rest.
[01:05] Samira: Great, that maps to what we saw. For Veridian, sounds like Private or Dedicated will be a stronger fit because of the PHI/data residency ask. For Nimbus, hosted with Dedicated reserved capacity can work if we meet latency SLOs. For Lattice we need to confirm encryption/KMS and possibly HSM requirements.
[01:26] Jasper: Quick note — Veridian will want on-prem or VPC peering, they mentioned an air-gapped option if required. How does Redwood handle air-gapped?
[01:35] Ethan: Right now Redwood Private supports VPC and an on-prem package for highly regulated customers. There's some deployment work but it's an established flow; we have a checklist. I'll share the runbook.
[01:45] Miguel: Perfect. Also, pricing sensitivity — Veridian expects a pilot under $60k for 3 months.
[01:52] Samira: Understood. We'll size the pilot and suggest a Dedicated pool with capped burst so cost is predictable. Ethan, can you ballpark tokens per minute for the summarization workload?
[02:05] Ethan: Off the cuff, if they're doing clinical notes summarization at medium length, maybe 1200-2500 input tokens per request with generation ~200 tokens avg. If concurrency is 5–10, that pushes us toward 2–4 GPUs for steady throughput depending on model choice. But I'll run numbers and send a quick capacity estimate.
[02:28] Priya: On models, Veridian asked about model provenance and fine-tuning. Do you support customer fine-tunes or is it adapters?
[02:36] Samira: We offer model variants and a few finetuning paths — majority of customers use prompt engineering + adapters, but for Private/Dedicated customers we can discuss fine-tune access. Note: model names in docs are sometimes abbreviated, and we've seen transcription of those go wrong in notes, just a heads up.
[02:51] Miguel: Haha, yes, last time our notes said KV cache and someone wrote "K V cake" in the doc.
[02:56] Ethan: (laughs) Classic.
[03:00] Samira: Moving on — Nimbus Retail, call center bot. Priority is latency under 300ms p95 for the short queries. For that workload, a quantized L2+ model on Dedicated can usually meet it. Jasper, any other constraints?
[03:15] Jasper: They want the bot integrated with Genesys and real-time call piping. We need a stable streaming API and request/response correlation for transcripts. Is Redwood streaming stable for that?
[03:25] Ethan: Yes, streaming is supported; we also have tracing hooks in Redwood Console to map tokens and latency per request. Integration patterns with Genesys are common but we'll need to prototype.
[03:35] Priya: For Lattice Finance, they flagged SOC2 and a requirement for KMS integration. Do you have a standard KMS/HSM integration?
[03:44] Samira: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated support KMS integrations; HSM option exists for enterprise. We'll attach the compliance pack and SOC2 report after this call.
[03:55] Miguel: Good. Quick question on attribution — for co-sell, how will leads be routed? We'll need clear handoff rules and revenue crediting.
[04:05] Samira: We usually capture attribution in the co-sell spreadsheet and CRM. We'll propose lead routing rules (partner-source, AE handoff) and share a draft.
[04:16] Miguel: Perfect.
[04:20] Samira: Okay I'll switch to the pipeline worksheet that Miguel sent earlier. (screen-share note) The three deals are marked green, yellow, red by expected close date. Veridian is green for pilot interest, Nimbus is yellow, Lattice is red pending procurement.
[04:36] Priya: For Lattice, procurement is the blocker; they want preapproved legal terms.
[04:41] Samira: Understood, legal can expedite an SPA once we have logos. We'll coordinate.
[04:50] Ethan: Quick technical flag — for Veridian if they insist on on-prem, we need to clarify latency expectations and how much data leaves their environment; Private can be configured to keep inference inside their VPC. Also caching (prefix/KV cache) will help reduce cost, but for PHI we should confirm retention policies.
[05:12] Miguel: Retention must be zero or reversible encryption after 30 days.
[05:18] Ethan: Okay, we can include that in the security checklist.
[05:22] Samira: On competitors, Miguel said Veridian is talking to CloudAI and ModelServe. Their big pitch is price but limited enterprise controls. We should emphasize our SSO, audit logs, and dedicated deployment options.
[05:35] Miguel: Yup.
[05:38] Priya: Any recent wins or reference customers we can share for healthcare?
[05:42] Samira: We have a health system pilot (anonymized) that showed improved coding throughput; I'll share a redacted case study and the benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:50] Miguel: That helps.
[05:52] Samira: Alright, on procurement and timelines — Miguel you mentioned 6 weeks for Veridian decision. For our part, we'll need exec sponsor intro and legal contacts. Can you share stakeholder emails?
[06:04] Miguel: Yes, I'll share by EOD.
[06:07] Samira: Excellent.
[06:10] -- Transcript skips ahead to tech deep-dive --
[15:05] Ethan: Back to the technical checks — Jasper, can you confirm expected concurrency and average request size for Veridian?
[15:12] Jasper: Concurrency is unknown but expected spikes during end-of-day batch summarization; maybe up to 20 concurrent for peak. Average note size 2k tokens.
[15:22] Ethan: Okay that pushes the pilot sizing; could be CPU and GPU heavy. For Dedicated, we can configure autoscale and burst to handle spikes but there will be cost tradeoffs. I'll include a few scenarios in my estimate.
[15:35] Jasper: Good. Also, for the Genesys integration on Nimbus — we need webhooks to map real-time transcript segments back to the CRM. Does Redwood have webhook recommender?
[15:45] Ethan: We have webhook hooks and streaming events; integration patterns vary but we've built connectors before. We'll provide sample code.
[15:53] Priya: On security docs — can you send SOC2, penetration test summary, and data flow diagrams?
[15:59] Samira: Yes, we'll attach SOC2 and a pen-test summary and the data flow. Expect those in the follow-up email.
[16:06] Miguel: Great.
[16:08] Samira: Competitor note — VendorX undercuts on price but lacks KMS/HSM and dedicated SLAs; that might be a wedge.
[16:18] Miguel: Noted.
[16:20] -- Closing and recap --
[25:00] Samira: Alright quick recap: Samira to send pricing/SOW and redacted case study; Ethan to send capacity estimates and sample integration code; Miguel to share stakeholder contacts and top pilot logos; Jasper to send dataset examples and security constraints. We'll meet next week to align on the pilot SOW.
[25:19] Priya: Works for us.
[25:22] Miguel: One more ask — can Redwood provide a short demo for Veridian execs showing data residency controls?
[25:29] Samira: Yes, can do. We'll schedule a 20–30 minute exec demo; Samira to coordinate dates.
[25:36] Jasper: Thanks all.
[25:38] Ethan: I'll follow up on the runbook and send the Dedicated sizing scenarios.
[25:43] Samira: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

Shared artifacts mentioned in call:
- Partner pipeline spreadsheet (Miguel) - link noted in calendar
- Redwood co-sell playbook deck (shared by Samira)
- SOC2 and security pack (to be sent)
- Benchmark spreadsheet for healthcare pilot (to be shared)

Notes on transcript quality: audio had a short drop at ~00:50 which garbled a sentence, and proper nouns (model names, KV cache) were mistranscribed in a few places.
